images.author: Hugo Sykes
images.why: Common hippopotamus grazing on land in Narok, Kenya; strong habitat and body-view candidate. Mouth closed; native dimensions and exact 9:10 crop unverified.

images.author: Hugo Sykes
images.why: Alternative land photograph of a wild common hippo in Kenyan savanna. Open surroundings offer cropping flexibility; sex and native dimensions unverified.

images.author: Adriaan Greyling
images.why: 6609 × 4409 photograph of a hippo grazing beside a river, with birds and lush vegetation. Environmental alternative; animal prominence after a 9:10 crop needs checking.

images.author: Robin Moore / Global Wildlife Conservation
images.why: Authentic Javan rhino in Ujung Kulon's forest wallow, published by a specialist conservation organisation. Strong rare-species candidate; native dimensions unverified.

images.author: Robin Moore
images.why: Photographer's firsthand account establishes wild Ujung Kulon provenance. Rare encounter photograph; supplied version is only 1024 × 683, below the preferred resolution.

images.author: Stephen Belcher Photography / WWF
images.why: Documented Javan rhino photographed in water, with distinctive skin and horn detail. Partial-body fallback for this exceptionally rare species; native dimensions unverified.

images.author: Eddy Odingo Odira
images.why: 6000 × 4000 safari photograph from Nairobi National Park, Kenya. Single giraffe in savanna habitat; sex and hooves-to-ossicones crop need visual confirmation.

images.author: Nad Hemnani
images.why: Photographer titles this giraffe 'Old Boy'; photographed at Oserengoni Wildlife Sanctuary, Kenya. Promising adult-male candidate; native dimensions and exact framing unverified.

images.author: Giovanni Nicolini
images.why: Solitary giraffe in open savanna at Tsavo East National Park, Kenya. Uncluttered habitat candidate for a poster; sex and native dimensions unverified.

images.author: NIR HIMI
images.why: Source identifies a black rhinoceros standing in Etosha National Park, Namibia; Sony camera metadata supports photographic provenance. Lip detail, full-body framing and native dimensions remain unverified.

images.author: Yg pixel
images.why: 5760 × 3840 photograph identified by the source as wild Diceros bicornis in Tanzania. Natural vegetation setting; source calls it a close-up, so full-body framing and hooked lip need visual confirmation.

images.author: Subhadip Kanjilal
images.why: Photographer explicitly identifies this as a wild gaur in Jaldapara National Park, India, despite the generic page title. Standing forest-path candidate; sex, native dimensions and exact crop unverified.

images.author: Saketh Upadhya
images.why: Photographer identifies the grazing animal as gaur in Ooty, Tamil Nadu, rather than domestic cattle. Green habitat alternative; mature-bull status, native dimensions and full-body crop unverified.

images.author: Prashant S. Gupta
images.why: Photographer documents a dominant wild bull at Bandhavgarh, with dorsal ridge, curved horns and white lower legs. Strong subject match, though branches obscure parts of the animal; resolution unverified.
